If 𝑓 is continuous at 𝑥 = 0, then 𝑐1+𝑐2 = _________. (answer in integer)

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q10
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: Circles C1, C2, and C3, with centers O1, O2, and O3, and radii r1, r2, and r3, respectively, touch each other as shown in the following figure. Given r1 = 2 cm, r2 = 1 cm and the angle ∠O1O3O2 is 90°, r3 = _____ cm.
solution: Because the circles touch externally, the distance between any two centers equals the sum of their radii: \(O_1O_3 = r_1 + r_3 = 2 + r_3\), \(O_2O_3 = r_2 + r_3 = 1 + r_3\), and \(O_1O_2 = r_1 + r_2 = 3\). The angle \(\angle O_1O_3O_2 = 90^\circ\) makes \(\triangle O_1O_3O_2\) right-angled at \(O_3\), so the Pythagorean theorem gives \((2 + r_3)^2 + (1 + r_3)^2 = 3^2\). Expanding: \(4 + 4r_3 + r_3^2 + 1 + 2r_3 + r_3^2 = 9\), i.e. \(2r_3^2 + 6r_3 - 4 = 0\), or \(r_3^2 + 3r_3 - 2 = 0\). By the quadratic formula, \(r_3 = \tfrac{1}{2}(-3 \pm \sqrt{17})\); since a radius is positive, \(r_3 = \tfrac{1}{2}(-3 + \sqrt{17})\) cm.

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q3
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text:
A school has 100 students distributed among 1st to 10th standards.

Based on this, which one of the following statements is always correct?

options.html: There are at least 10 students who belong to the same standard.
There is at least one student in each standard.
There are at most 10 students in 10th standard.
The total number of students from 1st to 5th standards is at least 50.

solution: Distributing \(100\) students among \(10\) standards guarantees that some standard contains at least \(\lceil 100/10 \rceil = 10\) students by the pigeonhole principle.

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q4
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: How many 3-digit numbers can be formed using three distinct single digit prime numbers?
solution: The single-digit prime numbers are \(2, 3, 5,\) and \(7\). To form a 3-digit number using three distinct such digits, choose and arrange three of the four digits: \(4 \times 3 \times 2 = 24\).

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q10
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text:
As shown in the figure, circle C1 with center O1 and radius r1 touches the square VWXY at points P and Q while circle C2 with center O2 and radius r2 touches the square VWXY at points R and S. The two circles touch each other at T.

Given r1 = 1 cm and \(\overline{VY} = \overline{VW} = 4\text{ cm}\), r2 = _____ cm.
solution: Place the square on a coordinate plane with \(W=(0,0)\), \(X=(4,0)\), \(Y=(4,4)\), \(V=(0,4)\). Circle \(C_1\) (radius \(r_1=1\)) is tangent to the left and bottom sides, so its center is \(O_1=(1,1)\). Circle \(C_2\) (radius \(r_2\)) is tangent to the right and top sides, so its center is \(O_2=(4-r_2,\,4-r_2)\). Since the circles touch externally at \(T\), the distance between centers equals the sum of the radii: \(O_1O_2 = r_1+r_2 = 1+r_2\). Computing the squared distance: \((4-r_2-1)^2+(4-r_2-1)^2 = 2(3-r_2)^2\). Thus \(2(3-r_2)^2=(1+r_2)^2\). Taking the positive square root (as \(r_2<3\)): \(\sqrt{2}(3-r_2)=1+r_2\), giving \(3\sqrt{2}-1 = r_2(1+\sqrt{2})\), so \(r_2=\frac{3\sqrt{2}-1}{1+\sqrt{2}}\). Rationalizing by multiplying by \(\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}-1}\): numerator \((3\sqrt{2}-1)(\sqrt{2}-1)=6-3\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{2}+1=7-4\sqrt{2}\), denominator \((1+\sqrt{2})(\sqrt{2}-1)=1\). Hence \(r_2 = 7-4\sqrt{2}\) cm (about \(1.34\) cm).

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q7
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text:
The table lists the unit selling price of five products P, Q, R, S, and T. On a particular day, 250 items were sold with the average selling price of Rs. 60. The following observations were made:

(i) The quantity of S sold was twice that of T.

(ii) The quantity of R sold was thrice that of T.

(iii) The quantity of Q sold was four times that of T.

Product

P

Q

R

S

T

Unit selling price (Rs.)

100

50

40

60

60

What is the quantity of product P sold on that day?
solution: Let the quantity of T sold be \(x\). Then \(S=2x\), \(R=3x\), and \(Q=4x\). The total quantity gives \(P+4x+3x+2x+x=250\), so \(P=250-10x\). The total revenue is \(100P+50(4x)+40(3x)+60(2x)+60x=100P+500x\). Since the average selling price is Rs. 60 for 250 items, the total revenue is \(250 \times 60=15000\). Substituting \(P=250-10x\) gives \(100(250-10x)+500x=15000\), so \(25000-500x=15000\) and \(x=20\). Therefore \(P=250-10(20)=50\).

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q8
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: Consider a string P of length l that is laid out as a straight-line segment. Another string K is laid out as a semicircular arc with string P as its diameter, as represented in Figure (i). When both the strings are shortened by a length x they can be re-arranged such that the shortened string K forms a full circle with the shortened string P as its diameter, as represented in Figure (ii). The value of x/l is __________
solution: In Figure (i), string P has length \(l\) and string K is a semicircular arc of diameter \(l\), so its length is half a circumference: \(K = \tfrac{1}{2}\pi l\). After both are shortened by \(x\), the new lengths are \(P' = l - x\) and \(K' = \tfrac{\pi l}{2} - x\). In Figure (ii), the shortened K forms a full circle whose diameter is the shortened P, so its length equals the full circumference: \(K' = \pi P' = \pi(l - x)\). Equating the two expressions for \(K'\): \(\tfrac{\pi l}{2} - x = \pi l - \pi x\). Collecting terms gives \(\pi l - \tfrac{\pi l}{2} = \pi x - x\), i.e. \(\tfrac{\pi l}{2} = x(\pi - 1)\). Therefore \(\dfrac{x}{l} = \dfrac{\pi}{2(\pi - 1)}\).

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q3
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: At how many points will the curves y = x2 and y = -x2 - 2x - 1 intersect in the real (x, y) plane?
solution: Set \(x^2 = -x^2 - 2x - 1\), giving \(2x^2 + 2x + 1 = 0\). Its discriminant is \(\Delta = 2^2 - 4(2)(1) = -4 < 0\), so there are no real solutions. Therefore the curves intersect at 0 real points.

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q7
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: In the given figure, \(\overline{PQ}\) is the diameter of a circle with center O. Two points R and S are chosen on the circle such that \(\angle ROS = 80^\circ\). When \(\overline{PR}\) and \(\overline{QS}\) are extended, they meet at T. The value of \(\angle RTS\) is _________________
solution: Since \(PQ\) is a diameter, the central angles on the upper semicircle satisfy \(\angle POR + \angle ROS + \angle SOQ = 180^\circ\), so \(\angle POR + \angle SOQ = 180^\circ - 80^\circ = 100^\circ\). In triangle \(TPQ\), the angle at \(T\) equals \(\angle RTS\). The base angle \(\angle TPQ = \angle RPQ\) is an inscribed angle standing on arc \(RQ\) (not containing \(P\)), so \(\angle RPQ = \tfrac{1}{2}\angle ROQ = \tfrac{1}{2}(\angle ROS + \angle SOQ) = \tfrac{1}{2}(80^\circ + \angle SOQ)\). Likewise \(\angle TQP = \angle SQP = \tfrac{1}{2}\angle SOP = \tfrac{1}{2}(80^\circ + \angle POR)\). Adding these gives \(\angle RPQ + \angle SQP = \tfrac{1}{2}(160^\circ + \angle POR + \angle SOQ) = \tfrac{1}{2}(160^\circ + 100^\circ) = 130^\circ\). Hence \(\angle RTS = 180^\circ - 130^\circ = 50^\circ\).

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q10
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text:
P and Q are two positive integers such that P2 = Q2 + 13.

The product of the numbers P and Q is _________
solution: Rewrite the condition as \(P^2 - Q^2 = 13\), so \((P-Q)(P+Q)=13\). Since 13 is prime and \(P>Q>0\), the only positive factorization is \(P-Q=1\) and \(P+Q=13\). Solving gives \(P=7\) and \(Q=6\), hence \(PQ=42\).

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q2
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: The product of the digits of a three-digit number is 70. The sum of the digits of this three-digit number is _____
solution: Let the digits be a, b, and c. Their product is 70 = 2 × 5 × 7. Since each digit must be a single digit from 0 to 9, and the product is nonzero, the only possible digit multiset is 2, 5, 7. Their sum is 2 + 5 + 7 = 14.

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q4
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
subtopic: Laws or Properties or Rules of Logarithms
text: Consider two distinct positive real numbers m, n, with m > n. Let x = nlog10(m) and y = mlog10(n). The relation between x and y is _______.
solution: Let a=log10(m) and b=log10(n). Then m=10a and n=10b. Hence x=na=(10b)a=10ab and y=mb=(10a)b=10ab. Therefore x=y.

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q7
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
subtopic: Mean, Median, and Mode for ungrouped data
text: Five integers are picked from 0 to 20, with possible repetitions, such that their mean is 12, median is 18, and they have a single mode of 20. Ignoring permutations, the number of ways to pick these five integers is _____
solution: Let the sorted integers be a≤ b≤ c≤ d≤ e. The median gives c=18, and the mean gives a+b+c+d+e=60. Since 20 is the unique mode, it must occur more often than any other value. Because the median is 18, at most two entries can exceed 18, so 20 can occur at most twice. To be a mode, 20 must occur at least twice, hence exactly twice: d=e=20. Then a+b+18+20+20=60, so a+b=2. The other values must each occur at most once, so a<b<18. The only nonnegative integer solution is a=0 and b=2. Thus the only unordered selection is {0,2,18,20,20}, giving 1 way.

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q10
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: In the given figure, P, Q, and R are three points on a circle of radius 10 cm with O as its center, PQ = RQ, and ∠ PQR = 45°. The figure is representative. The area of the shaded region PQRO is ______________ cm2.
solution: Let the radius be r = 10. The inscribed angle ∠ PQR = 45° subtends arc PR, so the central angle ∠ POR = 2 × 45° = 90°. Because PQ = RQ, the figure is symmetric about the line QO. The shaded quadrilateral PQRO is concave at O; drawing the symmetry axis QO splits it into two congruent triangles QPO and QRO. Take QO = r = 10 as the base of each. With O at the origin and Q at the top, the radius OP lies 45° from the downward vertical (half of the 90° central angle), so the perpendicular distance from P to the line QO is \(10\cos 45^\circ = 5\sqrt{2}\). Hence each triangle has area \(\tfrac{1}{2} \cdot 10 \cdot 5\sqrt{2} = 25\sqrt{2}\), and the shaded area is \(2 \times 25\sqrt{2} = 50\sqrt{2}\) cm2. (Equivalently, area of △ QPR minus area of △ POR gives \((50 + 50\sqrt{2}) - 50 = 50\sqrt{2}\).)

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q4
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: Real numbers y, p, and n (all greater than 1) satisfy \((\log_{p^{1/n}} y)(\log_{y^{1/n}} p) = 16\), where the logarithms are taken to the bases \(p^{1/n}\) and \(y^{1/n}\). The value of n is ________
solution: By change of base, \(\log_{p^{1/n}}y=n\frac{\ln y}{\ln p}\) and \(\log_{y^{1/n}}p=n\frac{\ln p}{\ln y}\). Multiplying gives \(n^2=16\). Since \(n>1\), we obtain \(n=4\).

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q8
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: Let Pk represent the perimeter of a square with sides of length k. The value of the expression P1 + P2 + P3 + ··· + P10 is __________
solution: A square has four equal sides, so \(P_k=4k\). Thus, \(P_1+\cdots+P_{10}=4(1+\cdots+10)=4\cdot\frac{10\cdot11}{2}=220\).

title: GATE 2026 General Aptitude Q9
subject: Mathematics and Aptitude
text: The city of Atlantis was crafted by the God of the seas, Poseidon. It was made of alternating concentric circular rings of land (shaded) and water (not shaded) as represented in the figure (not to scale). The radius of Inner Island was 2.5 stades (a unit of length used in ancient Greece). The water surrounding Inner Island was one stade wide (length AB). This was surrounded by two pairs of alternating rings of land and water. The first pair of land and water was two stades wide each (lengths BC and CD), and the outer pair is three stades wide each (lengths DE and EF). The ratio of the surface area of the land to that of the water in the city of Atlantis is _________ (round off to two decimal places).
solution: The successive radii are 2.5, 3.5, 5.5, 7.5, 10.5, and 13.5 stades. Using the annulus area formula, the total land area is \(\pi[2.5^2+(5.5^2-3.5^2)+(10.5^2-7.5^2)]=78.25\pi\). The water area is \(\pi[(3.5^2-2.5^2)+(7.5^2-5.5^2)+(13.5^2-10.5^2)]=104\pi\). The required ratio is \(\frac{78.25}{104}\approx0.75\).
